dimensions.label: Value innovation
dimensions.description: Does the company simultaneously drive down costs AND lift buyer value? Core Blue Ocean move — pursuing both usually creates uncontested space.

dimensions.label: Uncontested market space
dimensions.description: Is the company competing in a red ocean (crowded, price-driven) or a genuinely new/uncontested space where the rules aren't set yet?

dimensions.label: New demand creation
dimensions.description: Does the company convert non-customers into customers, or is it fighting for share within an existing pie?

dimensions.label: Distinctive strategic move
dimensions.description: Is there one identifiable big strategic move (product, model, geography) that defines the moat, or is the story incremental?

dimensions.label: Cost + value alignment
dimensions.description: Have they broken the value-cost trade-off through elimination / reduction / raising / creation of value elements?

dimensions.rationale: U.S. commercial revenue rose 149% y/y to $764M as AIP/Ontology let enterprises deploy operational AI on existing data without bespoke integration.
Analysts describe the market splitting into a high-security, high-switching-cost ontology layer where Palantir dominates versus a crowded general AI-tooling layer.
Record U.S. commercial TCV of $2.132B (+153% y/y) and 220 deals of at least $1M closed in the quarter reflect converting non-AI-adopting enterprises into customers.
The AIP Bootcamp go-to-market motion and the Ontology data layer are Palantir's singular defining bet, credited with 149% y/y U.S. commercial growth.
GAAP operating margin expanded to 47% from 27% a year ago as opex grew just 34.2% against 92.8% revenue growth — a real broken cost-value trade-off.

screens.verdict: Palantir's Ontology/AIP platform is converting non-AI-adopting enterprises into customers (record $2.132B U.S. commercial TCV, +153% y/y) while margin expanded to 47% from 27% — the batch's strongest composite.

sources.ref: How Palantir is Turning AI Into Mission-Critical Infrastructure (finance.yahoo.com)

dimensions.rationale: Gross margin of 74.9% on $81.62B quarterly revenue shows pricing power on accelerated-computing platforms, with Data Center at $75.2B (+92% y/y) on the Blackwell ramp.
Data Center revenue of $75.2B is +92% y/y, and the filing cites InfiniBand, Spectrum-X and NVLink demand alongside GPUs, a full-stack AI infrastructure category.
Total revenue rose 85.2% y/y to $81.62B on AI and accelerated-computing demand, while Edge Computing added $6.4B (+29% y/y).
Blackwell remained the majority of Data Center shipments this quarter, and operating income rose 147.4% y/y to $53.54B against revenue growth of 85.2%.
Operating expenses rose 52% y/y, slower than revenue growth of 85%, and gross margin of 74.9% was roughly flat q/q, so the value-cost gap is wide but the gain is mostly pricing.

screens.verdict: Platform-level AI infrastructure position with 85% y/y revenue growth and a 74.9% gross margin gives a composite of 72, though margin strength reflects pricing power more than cost reduction.

dimensions.rationale: AWS operating margin was 39.4% versus 32.9% a year earlier on $42.2B revenue (+37% y/y), raising customer scale while improving unit economics.
AWS grew 37% y/y, its fastest pace in 18 quarters, but it competes with other hyperscalers; North America grew 16% and International 15% in contested retail.
Net sales rose 19.6% y/y to $200.6B, and management cited continued AWS and AI momentum when guiding Q3 net sales to $197.0B-$202.0B.
Retail plus AWS flywheel: AWS operating income rose 64% y/y to $16.6B, providing most of the consolidated gain of 43.2% to $27.5B.
Operating income grew 43.2% against revenue growth of 19.6%, but TTM free cash flow swung to a $7.6B outflow as capex rose $66.1B y/y for AI infrastructure.

screens.verdict: AWS reacceleration to 37% growth at a 39.4% margin lifts operating income 43.2% y/y, while a $7.6B TTM free-cash-flow outflow and a one-time Anthropic gain temper the composite at 68.

dimensions.rationale: Value-added services revenue rose 20% y/y within $9.28B net revenue, adding security/data value atop the core network without raising buyer cost.
Agent Pay for Machines, a machine-to-machine payment rail with 30+ launch users (Adyen, Coinbase, Cloudflare), stakes out an uncontested agentic space.
Cross-border volume grew 12% and GDV 8% on existing card usage; agentic-commerce products are early (Malaysia pilot), not yet a proven demand driver.
CEO Miebach is positioning Mastercard's tokenization and identity infrastructure to set the trust standard for agentic commerce, a distinctive bet.
Operating margin expanded to 60.2% from 58.7% as opex grew only 10% against 14% revenue growth.

screens.verdict: Mastercard is stacking value-added services (+20% y/y) and early agentic-commerce infrastructure atop its network, expanding margin to 60.2% while entering an uncontested machine-payment space.

sources.ref: Mastercard Q2 Earnings Call Highlights Agentic Commerce Push (finance.yahoo.com)

dimensions.rationale: Q1 FY2027 gross margin rose 6bps on mix shift toward higher-margin businesses like advertising while eCommerce grew 26% — layering higher-margin digital revenue atop everyday-low-price retail is a cost-down/value-up combination.

Same-day fulfillment from over 8,400 of 10,900+ stores within roughly 10 miles of 90% of the US population is a structural advantage pure-play e-commerce rivals cannot easily replicate, per industry analysis.

Walmart+ membership exceeds 35 million subscribers and Walmart Connect is expanding advertiser integrations (Pacvue, Skai), converting shoppers into a recurring digital ecosystem beyond one-time retail transactions.
Repositioning 10,900+ stores as fulfillment hubs for a store-plus-digital omnichannel model is described industry-wide as Walmart's most significant transformation since founding.

Q1 FY2027 revenue rose 7.3% y/y to $177.8B on 4.3% Walmart U.S. and 5.9% Sam's Club comp sales while gross margin still improved 6bps — scale-driven low prices maintained alongside a rising higher-margin revenue mix.

screens.verdict: Walmart's Q1 FY2027 results (revenue +7.3% y/y, gross margin +6bps) show an ERRC pattern in motion — everyday-low-price retail layered with higher-margin advertising, membership and marketplace revenue via a fulfillment network rivals can't easily copy.

sources.ref: Walmart omnichannel / advertising strategic-positioning coverage (financialcontent.com, simplywall.st)

dimensions.rationale: Q2 FY2026 revenue rose 47.7% y/y to $22.97B on 60% worldwide volume growth even as realized prices fell 13% — value delivered (tirzepatide's efficacy) outpacing price, a genuine cost-down/value-up pattern.

Zepbound holds roughly 70% of new branded-obesity prescriptions per market reporting, but the category is fast-crowding with Novo Nordisk's Wegovy and upcoming oral entrants — leadership in an increasingly contested space.

Zepbound's FDA approval for obstructive sleep apnea and tirzepatide's pediatric/adolescent T2D approval expand the addressable patient pool beyond the original obesity/diabetes indications, converting new patient populations.

Orforglipron, an oral GLP-1, is set for a 2026 regulatory obesity filing per Q2 disclosures and industry reporting — one distinctive pipeline bet extending the metabolic-disease franchise beyond injectable tirzepatide.

Gross margin rose 150bps on production cost and mix in Q2 FY2026, but EPS growth (26.2% y/y) trailed revenue growth (47.7%) due to $2.8B of acquired IPR&D charges — premium pricing, not a value-cost realignment.

screens.verdict: Lilly's Q2 FY2026 revenue rose 47.7% y/y to $22.97B on 60% volume growth even as realized prices fell 13%, a genuine value-up/cost-down pattern in obesity care, though the category is fast-crowding with Novo Nordisk and new oral entrants.

sources.ref: Eli Lilly obesity-drug market positioning coverage (cnbc.com, biospace.com, nasdaq.com)

dimensions.rationale: Operating margin of 31.8% on $127.6B revenue (+25% y/y), with Google Cloud operating income more than tripling to $11.1B.
Google Cloud revenue rose 103% y/y to $30.7B, but Cloud competes against established hyperscalers and Search at $63.4B (+12%) is a mature, contested market.
Search query growth was the highest in five years, and Cloud revenue of $30.7B (+103% y/y) was lifted by enterprise AI solutions and TPU systems sales.
Full-stack AI approach, including TPU systems sales cited as a meaningful Cloud contributor; capex of $51.4B versus $24.0B a year earlier backs the move.
Operating income grew 30% to $40.6B versus revenue growth of 25%, though capex rose 114% y/y and diluted EPS fell to $2.12 from $2.87 on an equity-securities loss.

screens.verdict: Cloud revenue doubling to $30.7B and a 31.8% operating margin support a composite of 62, tempered by contested core markets and capex up 114% y/y.

dimensions.rationale: Operating margin of 31.8% on $127.6B revenue (+25% y/y), with Google Cloud operating income more than tripling to $11.1B.
Google Cloud revenue rose 103% y/y to $30.7B, but Cloud competes against established hyperscalers and Search at $63.4B (+12%) is a mature, contested market.
Search query growth was the highest in five years, and Cloud revenue of $30.7B (+103% y/y) was lifted by enterprise AI solutions and TPU systems sales.
Full-stack AI approach, including TPU systems sales cited as a meaningful Cloud contributor; capex of $51.4B versus $24.0B a year earlier backs the move.
Operating income grew 30% to $40.6B versus revenue growth of 25%, though capex rose 114% y/y and diluted EPS fell to $2.12 from $2.87 on an equity-securities loss.

screens.verdict: Same company as GOOGL: Cloud revenue doubling to $30.7B and a 31.8% operating margin support a composite of 62, tempered by contested core markets and capex up 114% y/y.

dimensions.rationale: Gross margin of 50.1% on $109.42B revenue (+16.4% y/y) with about 2 points from a one-off tariff-refund benefit, so the underlying margin is lower than reported.
Revenue grew double digits across iPhone, Mac and Services, but these are mature categories with established rivals; the release names no new market.
Revenue rose 16.4% y/y across every geographic segment, which suggests share and upgrade growth in existing categories rather than new non-customer demand.
Integrated hardware and Services ecosystem produced $54.77B gross profit (+25.3% y/y) and $62.09B of nine-month buybacks, funded by a distinctive platform model.
Cost of revenue grew 8.6% y/y against revenue growth of 16.4%, and operating income rose 26.6% to $35.70B, showing value rising faster than cost.

screens.verdict: Ecosystem model lifts operating income 26.6% y/y on 16.4% revenue growth, but categories are mature and about 2 points of margin came from a one-off tariff refund, for a composite of 62.

dimensions.rationale: Revenue of $90.0B (+17.7% y/y) with operating income up 18.3% to $40.6B; Microsoft 365 Copilot reached over 30 million paid seats per the CEO.
Azure grew 43% and Microsoft Cloud reached $59.3B (+27%), but both compete directly with other hyperscalers, while More Personal Computing fell 4%.
Microsoft 365 Copilot passed 30 million paid seats and Azure revenue surpassed $100B for the year, adding AI demand on top of existing enterprise customers.
Cloud plus AI bundling across Azure and Microsoft 365; quarterly EPS of $4.81 included a $0.27 per share lift from a $3.2B Anthropic investment gain and lower retirement costs.
Operating income grew 18.3% against revenue growth of 17.7%, but quarterly capex was $35.8B and Xbox severance and impairment charges offset part of the gain.

screens.verdict: Cloud and AI bundling drive 17.7% revenue growth and an 18.3% rise in operating income, but head-to-head hyperscaler competition and one-off gains hold the composite at 62.

dimensions.rationale: Gross margin of 69.5% (+1.5ppt y/y) and operating margin of 48.9% (+9.5ppt y/y) on $22.19B revenue (+47.9% y/y) show scale leverage from custom AI silicon.
AI semiconductor revenue was $10.8B (+143% y/y) in custom accelerators and networking, but infrastructure software grew just 9% y/y in a mature market.
Growth came from hyperscaler custom-accelerator and networking demand that management said outpaced its own forecast, serving existing large customers rather than new non-customers.
Custom AI accelerators drove semiconductor solutions up 79% y/y to $15.0B (68% of revenue), and Q3 revenue was guided to about $29.4B (+84% y/y).
Free cash flow was $10.26B (46% of revenue) on only $231M capex, and operating income rose 83.6% y/y against revenue growth of 47.9%.

screens.verdict: Custom AI silicon lifts revenue 47.9% y/y with a 48.9% operating margin, but concentration in existing hyperscaler customers and slow software growth hold the composite at 60.

dimensions.rationale: Revenue rose 25.5% y/y to $28,236M, but operating margin fell to 1.4% from 4.1% as R&D rose 49% and SG&A rose 45% y/y.
Management frames the quarter around Robotaxi, Cybercab and Optimus, which are not yet disclosed as revenue, while Megapack energy storage grew on higher deployments.
Cash deliveries rose about 25% y/y and FSD (Supervised) subscription revenue grew, though regulatory-credit revenue fell as government programs were restricted.
AI-program bet with 2026 capex guided to more than $25B; R&D spending jumped 49% y/y, but operating income fell 56.9% y/y to $398M.
Energy storage gross margin fell to 20.4% from 30.3% y/y on a lower average selling price and warranty adjustments, and net income was held flat by a $274M tax benefit.

screens.verdict: New-market ambitions in AI and robotics sit against a 1.4% operating margin and a 56.9% y/y fall in operating income, giving a composite of 55.

dimensions.rationale: MI400-series Instinct GPUs (MI455X specced at 40 petaflops FP4, 432GB HBM4) are positioned for enterprise buyers balancing performance and cost against Nvidia's dominant share — a value angle within, not outside, the existing accelerator cost curve.
Nvidia holds an estimated ~80% of AI-accelerator revenue ($193.7B FY2026) versus AMD's estimated 5-7% share — a highly contested market despite Q2 FY2026 Data Center revenue of $6.7B, up 107% y/y.

AMD is targeting smaller enterprise customers priced out of Nvidia's top-tier GPUs, per industry reporting, aiming to convert cost-sensitive AI buyers who are otherwise non-consumers of frontier-scale accelerators.

Shift from selling standalone chips to selling full rack-scale systems (Helios, cited at 3 AI exaflops per rack) is AMD's identifiable strategic pivot, alongside Q2 FY2026 Data Center revenue of $6.7B, 58% of total revenue.
Q2 FY2026 gross margin rose to 54% from a year-ago quarter depressed by an $800M MI308 export-control charge — a base-effect comparison, not an evidenced structural cost advantage over Nvidia.

screens.verdict: AMD's Q2 FY2026 Data Center revenue more than doubled to $6.7B, but the AI-accelerator market remains dominated by Nvidia's roughly 80% share — AMD's rack-scale systems pivot is a distinctive move within a still-contested category, not an uncontested one.

sources.ref: AMD Instinct MI400 / Nvidia AI-accelerator competitive-share coverage (wccftech.com, siliconanalysts.com)

dimensions.rationale: Skyrizi (+24.4% y/y to $5.51B) and Rinvoq (+24.5% y/y to $2.53B) deliver differentiated efficacy over biosimilar Humira, raising clinical value at comparable cost.
Immunology is crowded — Humira itself now faces -35.9% y/y biosimilar erosion, proof the category is contested, not uncontested.
The $10.9B Apogee acquisition adds zumilokibart (IL-13, atopic dermatitis) and APG273 (IL-13/TSLP, asthma) into adjacent but already-established disease categories.
The $10.9B Apogee Therapeutics acquisition is AbbVie's defining post-Humira move, adding late-stage candidates to sustain the Skyrizi/Rinvoq growth engine.
GAAP operating margin of 37.9% and adjusted diluted EPS growth of 22.9% y/y reflect margin execution, not a broken cost-value trade-off.

screens.verdict: AbbVie is replacing Humira's biosimilar-eroded revenue ($756M, -35.9% y/y) with higher-efficacy Skyrizi/Rinvoq franchises and the $10.9B Apogee bolt-on, a value-raising but crowded strategy.

dimensions.rationale: AI-infrastructure product orders reached $5.3B year-to-date as Cisco bundles silicon, security and software, raising buyer value but not clearly lowering unit cost.
Cisco competes against Arista, Juniper (under HPE) and hyperscaler-native networking solutions — a mapped, contested infrastructure market.
FY2026 AI-infrastructure revenue outlook was raised to $4B from $3B on hyperscaler orders — capturing existing AI-capex spend, not creating new demand.
Deepening collaboration with NVIDIA to position as agentic-era AI infrastructure, plus embedding security into networking, is Cisco's defining move.
GAAP operating margin expanded to 25.0% from about 22.6% as opex rose just 1% against 12% revenue growth.

screens.verdict: Cisco is bundling silicon, security and software into AI-ready infrastructure ($5.3B of AI orders YTD) with margin expanding to 25.0%, but operates in a well-mapped market against Arista and Juniper.

sources.ref: AI, security tailwinds signal promising 2026 for Cisco (networkworld.com)

dimensions.rationale: Innovative Medicine grew 7.8% and MedTech 4.5%; bundling pharma and devices raises buyer value but doesn't restructure the cost curve.
J&J competes head-to-head with Merck in oncology, Pfizer in immunology, and Roche in diagnostics — a mapped, contested landscape.
FDA approval of ICOTYDE (April 2026) targets disease categories already served by Skyrizi/Rinvoq-class drugs — incremental, not new demand.
The Kenvue consumer-health spin-off refocused J&J into a pure dual-pillar Innovative Medicine + MedTech company, its defining structural move.
Gross margin expanded 32bp y/y to 68.2% on operational leverage — a modest gain, not a structural cost-value breakthrough.

screens.verdict: J&J's post-Kenvue dual Innovative Medicine + MedTech model bundles pharma and device innovation but competes in crowded categories against Pfizer, Merck and Roche.

sources.ref: Johnson & Johnson's New Era of Growth (kavout.com)

dimensions.rationale: Ad price per impression rose 12% y/y even as impressions grew 14% y/y (both company-disclosed), and Reality Labs posted a $4.62B quarterly operating loss with no near-term buyer-value payoff — mixed evidence against a clean value-innovation read.
The core advertising business competes directly with Google, Amazon and TikTok for the same advertiser budgets — not uncontested space.

Llama's open-weights distribution (Llama 5 shipped April 2026 per industry reporting) aims to make Meta's model layer the default developer substrate, a demand-creation play distinct from the core ad auction.

Meta split its AI strategy in April 2026, shipping Llama 5 as open-weights alongside a closed Muse Spark model (per industry reporting) — a distinctive bet to commoditize the model layer while ring-fencing its ad-targeting edge.

Total costs and expenses rose 55% y/y on $2.40B of legal-proceedings charges and $1.18B of severance (company-disclosed), compressing operating margin from 43% to 31% this quarter — a clear cost/value deterioration, not alignment.

screens.verdict: Core ad business grew 28% y/y but operating margin compressed 12ppt on legal and severance charges, while a dual-track open/closed Llama strategy targets AI-adjacent demand creation — a contested core market weighs down a distinctive model-layer bet.

dimensions.rationale: Q2 FY2026 revenue rose 14.4% y/y to $11.63B on transaction/volume growth within Visa's existing fee-based network model — no disclosed cost-down mechanism for merchants or consumers accompanies this growth.

Card-network payments remain a Visa/Mastercard duopoly; Visa's stablecoin response has been to integrate them as an on/off-ramp rail rather than operate in a category free of Mastercard and blockchain-native competitors.

A stated OpenAI partnership aims to embed Visa payments in AI-driven agentic commerce, a nascent transaction category, though it extends existing rails to new use cases rather than reaching new non-card-using customers.

Visa cited $13B in annual technology investment at its 2026 Payments Forum to reposition from transaction processor to commerce orchestrator, spanning AI, stablecoin settlement and tokenization initiatives.

Q2 FY2026 net income rose only 6.8% y/y, below 14.4% revenue growth, as operating income growth of 15.4% partly compressed toward the bottom line — no disclosed reduction in Visa's fee-based merchant cost structure.

screens.verdict: Visa's Q2 FY2026 revenue growth (+14.4% y/y to $11.63B) came from expanding transaction volume within an unchanged fee-based network model; its stablecoin and AI-commerce initiatives extend the existing moat rather than reset the payments cost-value curve.

sources.ref: Visa stablecoin / AI-commerce strategic-positioning coverage (pymnts.com, tradingview.com)

dimensions.rationale: Gross margin expanded to 84.6% from 37.7% y/y in Q2 FY2026 primarily on supply-constrained AI-memory pricing with 2026 HBM capacity sold out, reflecting oligopoly pricing power more than a cost-down/value-up product shift.
HBM remains a three-player oligopoly (Samsung, SK hynix, Micron); Micron held roughly 25% share in Q2 2026 versus SK hynix's lead — a concentrated, contested market rather than an uncontested one.

Growth rides external AI-datacenter buildout demand — Cloud Memory revenue more than doubled q/q to $13.77B in Q2 FY2026 — rather than Micron itself converting non-consumers into a new memory-buying segment.
Multi-year Strategic Customer Agreements plus HBM4 sample shipments and sold-out 2026 HBM capacity mark a distinctive supply-lock-in strategy as the only US-headquartered memory maker.
Q2 FY2026 margin expansion came from average-selling-price gains amid an industry supply shortage, not from cost reduction — the opposite of the ERRC cost-down half of the value-cost trade-off.

screens.verdict: Micron's record Q2 FY2026 margins (84.6% gross, up from 37.7% y/y) reflect an AI-memory supply shortage and oligopoly pricing power rather than a Blue Ocean cost-value breakthrough, in a market still contested by Samsung and SK hynix.

sources.ref: HBM market share / Micron AI memory 2026 competitive coverage (astutegroup.com, counterpointresearch.com)

dimensions.rationale: Q2 FY2026 revenue growth (+17.8% y/y reported, +28% per the release) was led by Markets trading (Equity Markets +86%) and IB fees — market-cycle-driven, not a cost-down/value-up shift in the banking product itself.

The stated $1.5 trillion Security and Resiliency Initiative financing defense, aerospace and supply chains is a differentiated niche within an otherwise saturated large-bank market, positioning JPM as a quasi-public financing partner.

Q2 FY2026 record net income ($21.2B) came from existing wholesale/markets and consumer segments; the planned 160-branch 2026 expansion targets share within the existing US banking market, not new non-banking customers.

160 planned new branches in 2026 (500 by 2027) is a distinctive counter-to-digital-trend move to deepen relationships via physical presence, paired with a stated ~$20B tech investment into underwriting and analytics.
Expense grew 15% y/y to $27.3B in Q2 FY2026, tracking higher compensation and technology spend — costs rose alongside revenue, with no disclosed value-cost realignment.

screens.verdict: JPMorgan's Q2 FY2026 profit jump (net income +41% y/y to $21.2B, including a $4.6B Visa share-exchange gain) reflects scale and market-cycle strength in an already-dominant, mature banking franchise rather than a Blue Ocean repositioning.

sources.ref: JPMorgan Chase 2026 branch expansion / moat coverage (pymnts.com, morningstar.com)

dimensions.rationale: Gross margin expanded 12.9ppt y/y to 40.4% on yield gains, but Intel Foundry still trails TSMC on process leadership, limiting value differentiation.
Intel Foundry competes directly against TSMC's dominant leading-edge share and Samsung — a highly contested, capital-intensive market.
Data Center and AI revenue rose 59% y/y and Foundry 31% y/y, both riding the existing hyperscaler AI-capex cycle rather than creating new demand.
IDM 2.0 opened Intel's fabs to external foundry customers, backed by a U.S. government equity stake giving a structural subsidy no rival has.
Restructuring charges fell to $170M from $1.89B y/y and R&D/MG&A spending declined 6%, cost discipline still in an early turnaround stage.

screens.verdict: Intel's IDM 2.0 foundry-opening strategy and government equity backing are a distinctive bet, but it remains a process-technology follower against TSMC in a highly contested foundry market.

sources.ref: Intel's IDM 2.0 Strategy: A Turnaround Play (gainseekers.com)

dimensions.rationale: $20B cumulative structural cost savings vs. 2019 lowers cost, but a commodity barrel of oil carries no differentiated buyer value.
Permian output above 1.8M boe/d competes directly with Chevron and Pioneer-legacy peers in a contested, commodity-priced basin.
Q2 revenue rose 34.5% q/q to $114.5B on price/volume recovery in existing refining and upstream markets, not new demand categories.
The Pioneer Natural Resources acquisition, targeting $3B+ of synergies, is XOM's defining move tightening its low-cost Permian position.
Cumulative structural cost savings vs. 2019 were raised to $20B, with Permian assets sitting at the low end of the global cost curve.

screens.verdict: ExxonMobil is a disciplined low-cost commodity operator ($20B of structural savings, Permian scale) but competes within existing oil markets rather than creating new demand or buyer value.

dimensions.rationale: Virtual assistant Erica has supported nearly 50 million users and 3 billion interactions, though the underlying universal-bank model matches big-bank peers.
BAC's universal-bank model directly overlaps JPMorgan, Citi and Wells Fargo across consumer, wealth and investment banking — a saturated category.
Investment banking fees jumped 50% and trading revenue rose 33% — both gains in fee pools that already existed, not newly created demand.
1,400 AI and machine-learning patents and Erica's near-50-million-user base are BAC's most distinctive asset, though peers run comparable digital programs.
Efficiency ratio improved 359bp y/y to 59%, producing 6.6% operating leverage as expense growth (+8%) trailed revenue growth (+15%).

screens.verdict: Bank of America's scale and Erica's nearly 50 million users deliver real operating leverage (359bp efficiency-ratio gain), but the universal-bank model overlaps JPMorgan, Citi and Wells Fargo in a mature category.

sources.ref: Bank of America: Business Model, SWOT Analysis, and Competitors 2026 (pitchgrade.com)

dimensions.rationale: Berkshire's model is capital allocation atop $177.5B of cost-free insurance float (Q2 2026), investing in existing-industry incumbents (BNSF, BHE, insurers) rather than restructuring any product's cost-value curve.
Operates across 90+ subsidiaries in mature, competitive industries (P&C insurance, freight rail, utilities, retail) with no disclosed entry into an uncontested category this quarter.

Q2 FY2026 net-earnings growth (+107.5% y/y to $25,667M) was driven by $12,684M of investment gains and the absence of a prior-year $3,760M Kraft Heinz impairment — portfolio accounting effects, not new-customer conversion.

Insurance float reached $177.5B (+$1.1B since year-end 2025) per Q2 2026 disclosures, Berkshire's long-standing structural source of low-cost capital funding capital-intensive units like BNSF and Berkshire Hathaway Energy.

Scale economics in BNSF and Berkshire Hathaway Energy provide typical capital-intensive cost advantages, but Q2 2026 insurance underwriting profit fell 13% y/y per reporting — no ERRC-style value-cost breakthrough evidenced.

screens.verdict: Berkshire's Q2 FY2026 profit surge (net earnings $25,667M, +107.5% y/y) was driven by investment gains and a float-funded capital-allocation model spanning mature industries — a value-investing engine, not a Blue Ocean value-innovation story.

sources.ref: Berkshire Hathaway insurance float / conglomerate moat coverage (fool.com, mlq.ai)
